sections.html:
The offices you call depend on where the house sits. Greenburgh has six villages, and everything outside them is unincorporated town land. The town lies in western Westchester County, with the Hudson River on its western edge, Yonkers to the south, Mount Pleasant to the north, and White Plains and Scarsdale to the east. About half of residents live in villages. The rest live in unincorporated areas such as Fairview, Greenville and Hartsdale, plus North Elmsford and South Ardsley.

The Building Department takes complaints only for the unincorporated area, and the Tax Department sends village residents to their own Village Hall for due dates. A seller in Tarrytown therefore checks two sets of offices, while a seller in Hartsdale deals mostly with the town.

The town's population was 94,537 in 2025, spread over 35,813 households, and 74.0% of homes are owner-occupied. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $697,100, median rent is $2,316, household income in the middle is $152,256, and the average commute is 34.4 minutes. At that price level, closing costs and the state's one percent charge on high-value homes both start to matter. A rent figure near $2,316 is also a useful yardstick if you are deciding between selling and keeping the house as a rental.

Commuting questions come up first with buyers. Metro-North's Hudson Line stops in Hastings-on-Hudson, Dobbs Ferry, Ardsley-on-Hudson, Irvington and Tarrytown, and the Harlem Line has a Hartsdale station. The Thruway, the Cross Westchester Expressway, the Saw Mill River, Bronx River and Sprain Brook parkways, US 9 and state routes 9A, 100 and 119 all pass through. Bee-Line buses serve the town.

The tax office bills for ten separate school districts, and the district printed on your bill changes the total from one street to the next. Get your current bill in hand before pricing the house.

sections.h2: Building permits to check before listing
sections.html:
The Building Department's FAQ puts it broadly: a permit is needed for construction, repair, improvement, modification or demolition. A new roof on a one or two family house counts, and structural roof changes need drawings sealed by a New York State architect or engineer.

  • Sheds of any size need a permit. Only one is allowed per lot, in the rear yard, no bigger than 150 square feet and 10 feet high.
  • Fences need no building permit up to six feet in a front or side yard and eight feet in the rear, with a 30 inch cap near corners.
  • Repaving an existing driveway needs nothing, but enlarging it does, and Public Works may also require a curb cut or right-of-way permit.
  • Pulling or abandoning a heating oil tank takes its own permit and inspection.
  • No residential zoning district lists short-term rentals as a permitted use.

If a buyer mentions a vacation rental, raise that last rule early. Applications are taken in person or by mail on weekdays at 177 Hillside Avenue, and the forms page has the current hours.

sections.h2: Property taxes and what happens at closing
sections.html:
The Receiver of Taxes bills for the county, the town, the fire districts and ten school districts, and calls itself the largest municipal collection agency in Westchester. Before closing, ask the office for a written balance and the next due date.

  • Make checks payable to the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes, 177 Hillside Avenue. Online card payments carry a variable fee, while ACH payments are free.
  • Liens can't be paid online and have to be settled at the Tax Office.
  • A new owner should call the office so future bills reach the right person. If you have moved out, send your new mailing address in writing.

Two state rules apply. A bill that never arrives doesn't cancel the tax or the interest (Real Property Tax Law section 922), and the Receiver can't waive a penalty (section 920).

Greenburgh assessment and collection dates
DateWhat happens
June 1Tentative assessment roll open to the public
Until September 15Board of Assessment Review decides appeals
September 15Roll becomes final
January 31, April 30, September 30Tax office open until 7 p.m. on the last payment day

The final roll is a snapshot, and later small claims changes don't alter it. Check your own line against what similar nearby houses sold for. A buyer's attorney will read the same record, and the Assessor's Office can answer questions about the latest figure.

sections.h2: What the Westchester County Clerk needs for a deed
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded by the Land Records Division of the Westchester County Clerk. Its recording guide asks for four pieces: a cover page made in the county's PREP system, a TP-584, an RP-5217 transfer report, and a payment cover page showing fees and tax.

State transfer tax is $2 per $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500, and the seller normally pays it. A house or condo for one to three families sold at $1,000,000 or more also owes a one percent mansion tax. The clerk's staff don't draft deeds or advise on them, so rely on your attorney for the document itself.

sections.h2: Selling with a lien or an open tax balance
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes don't block a sale, but they have to be settled by closing. Start by asking the Receiver of Taxes for a written balance. A lien is handled differently from an ordinary bill: it can't be paid online, so someone has to bring the payment to the Tax Office at 177 Hillside Avenue or send it by check made out to the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes. Your closing attorney normally arranges this and takes the amount from your proceeds.

The Receiver has no power to waive a penalty, so a late bill costs what it costs. If you are behind and the house needs work you can't afford, a direct purchase by a cash buyer can pay the balance at the table and still leave you something. Compare that figure with what a listing would bring after commission, repairs and the months of carrying costs.

When a village bill applies as well as the town bill, collect both. The village office, not the town, sets the due dates for village taxes, so call that Village Hall for its schedule.

Start with the property condition disclosure statement required by Real Property Law section 462. The buyer must receive it before any binding contract is signed.

  • Certificates of occupancy or completion for finished space, and permit records for recent work.
  • Town, county and school tax bills, plus a village bill if you live in a village.
  • A lender payoff letter and details of any lien.
  • Your STAR status, since the state asks owners to close a registration after a sale.

A cash buyer who takes the house as is can skip showings and repair negotiations, but title work, payoff and recording still take time. Ask for a written closing date and proof of funds with every offer.

faqs.q: Do village homes in Greenburgh use the town Building Department?
faqs.a: Generally not. The town department handles complaints only in the unincorporated part of Greenburgh. For a house in a village such as Tarrytown, ask the village hall about permits and due dates.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for a new roof in Greenburgh?
faqs.a: Yes. A roof covering replacement on a one or two family house needs a building permit with drawings, and a structural change needs plans from a New York State architect or engineer.

faqs.q: Can the next owner run a short-term rental from a Greenburgh house?
faqs.a: Short-term rentals aren't a permitted use in any residential zoning district. A buyer with that plan should confirm with the Building Department before closing.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies to a Greenburgh sale?
faqs.a: State tax is $2 for every $500 of price. The one percent mansion tax starts at $1,000,000 for one to three family homes and condos, and the buyer pays it.

faqs.q: Where do Greenburgh property tax payments go?
faqs.a: To the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes at 177 Hillside Avenue, which collects for the county, town, fire districts and ten school districts. Village residents follow their village's own schedule.
